quote: But you're just trying to pay some money. Is that your interest in solar?
stewart_read: The interest question is garbled and closed-ended, producing a flat 'Yeah. Yeah.' instead of the emotional anchor the schema calls for.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally keeping it light since the customer already self-identified as uninformed, but the schema requires 60+ seconds of depth here regardless.
coaching_implication: Rephrase as an open question — 'What got you looking into solar?' — and let the customer talk before restating it back.

quote: This was yeah. This was my highest bill ever that I mean, February was cold, though.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a direct bill-pain anchor unprompted and the rep does not reflect it back or use it to build urgency toward the appointment.
coaching_implication: This is the exact line to flip: 'Highest bill ever — that's exactly why we want to get this design in front of you fast.'

stewart_read: A brand-new roof removes the most common solar objection/DQ path and the rep correctly notes it, but doesn't tie it forward into momentum for booking.
coaching_implication: Could pair the new-roof fact with the bill pain later as a 'you're perfectly set up for this' close.

quote: a couple months ago, it was 830.
stewart_read: An 830 credit score is a strong qualification signal the rep acknowledges only with a generic 'Oh, that's nice.'
coaching_implication: Could be used to build customer confidence that they'll easily qualify for the program, reinforcing appointment value.

quote: Just last thing we need is a picture of, power bill.
stewart_read: Rep correctly runs the required bill-collection step for what appears to be a paid lead, and persists through multiple attempts to get usable data.
coaching_implication: Persistence was good; still needs a flip once the number/graph is captured.

quote: are you guys looking for installers by chance?
stewart_read: An unusual tangent — customer asks about employment with Ion — that further derails the call from solar substance; rep obliges by going to check rather than redirecting to the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be building rapport/goodwill intentionally, but it costs call time without advancing qualification or urgency.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge briefly and redirect: 'I'll pass that along — let's lock in your appointment first.'

quote: we I'm just double checking. March 18, 2PM.
stewart_read: Appointment date/time locked but button-up is only partial — no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction, no explicit 'is that fair' handshake.
coaching_implication: Add the missing button-up elements even on calls that feel casual and rapport-heavy — they protect show rate.
